artifact-00:
| Stop Category | IEC 60204-1 Definition | Motor Power | Brakes Applied | ISO 13850 / ISO 10218 Use | Behavior on Brakeless Arm (PiPER) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0** | Uncontrolled stop by immediate removal of power to the machine actuators; the resulting trajectory is not controlled. (pqac-00000001) | Removed immediately | Applied if fitted; PiPER has none | ISO 13850 permits category 0 or 1 for emergency stop, selected by risk assessment. ISO 10218 permits category 0 for protective stops and requires category 0 if a controlled deceleration fails or unintended motion occurs. (pqac-00000000) | Torque disappears immediately; gravity can back-drive loaded joints, so the arm may sag or drop. “Power off” is therefore not necessarily a mechanically safe state. Measure both pre-de-energization stopping travel and subsequent gravity-driven displacement. |
| **1** | Controlled stop with actuator power maintained during deceleration; power is removed after standstill and brakes are then applied. (pqac-00000001) | Maintained while stopping, then removed | Applied after standstill if fitted; none on PiPER | ISO 13850 permits category 1 emergency stop where controlled stopping reduces risk. ISO 10218 permits category 1 protective stops. (pqac-00000000) | Can stop the commanded motion smoothly, but after power removal the unbraked arm can still sag or fall. It is acceptable only if the arm reaches a supported or gravity-stable pose before de-energization, or another holding measure prevents descent. |
| **2** | Controlled stop with actuator power remaining available after standstill; brakes are not applied. (pqac-00000001) | Remains energized | Not applied | Not an emergency-stop category under ISO 13850. ISO 10218 can permit category 2 as a protective stop where continued energized holding is justified and monitored. (pqac-00000000) | Active torque can hold pose and avoid gravity drop, but safety depends on the controller, drives, communications, and supply remaining functional. It is unsuitable as the sole response to Pi reboot, supply loss, or emergency isolation and requires restart prevention plus monitored standstill. |


*Table: IEC 60204-1 stop categories mapped to ISO 13850/ISO 10218 usage and the gravity-drop consequences of PiPER’s brakeless joints. The table distinguishes stopping commanded motion from maintaining a safe state afterward.*
artifact-01:
| Test ID | Test Name | Standard/Source | What to Measure | Instruments | Minimum Repetitions | Acceptance Criterion | Records to Keep |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V-01 | E-stop functional test—magnetic supply switch | IEC 60204-1 stop categories; ISO 13850 principles; ISO 13849-2 validation; ISO 10218 protective stops. Category 0 immediately removes actuator power, after which an unbraked arm may descend. (pqac-00000000, pqac-00000001, pqac-00000027) | Time from actuation to supply loss; stopping time and distance; gravity-driven travel after power removal; hazardous motion; latch/reset and restart behavior; independence from Pi, CAN, network and IoT software. | Two-channel oscilloscope or logic analyzer monitoring switch and supply voltage; current probe; 60–240 fps calibrated video; ruler or laser distance meter. | At least **3 per condition**: empty and maximum intended payload, worst horizontal/downward poses, and maximum permitted speed; test each actuator and foreseeable fault separately. (pqac-00000002) | Every actuation removes power without software; hazardous commanded motion stops; reset alone cannot cause restart; the complete stopping-plus-drop envelope remains contained without impact, pinch, spill or payload release. Until passed, the switch must not be credited as an E-stop. | Protocol and date; wiring diagram; component IDs; raw traces and video; pose, speed, payload and tool; each result and maximum; anomalies, corrective actions and reviewer signatures. |
| V-02 | Power-loss gravity-drop characterization | ISO 12100 risk assessment and system-level validation under real-use conditions; back-drivable actuators can move under output loads after de-energization. No published PiPER-specific drop data were found. (pqac-00000005, pqac-00000027, pqac-00000029) | TCP and joint displacement from power loss to rest; peak downward speed; time to contact; final pose; payload retention; effects of pose, payload, mains loss, relay opening and CAN/controller failure. | High-frame-rate camera with calibrated scale; tracking software; optional joint/CAN logging and accelerometer; noninterfering catch sling, foam stop or support. | At least **3 per pose–payload condition**; use **5** where variation exceeds 10% or results approach a boundary. Test no load, typical load and maximum intended load in home, maximum-reach and task-critical poses. (pqac-00000043, pqac-00000045) | No person can occupy the measured fall/sweep envelope; no contact with printers, cameras, containers or enclosure; no payload release. Operation near people requires a support, brake, counterbalance or exclusion enclosure containing the worst result plus uncertainty and margin. | Joint angles and pose images; payload mass and center of mass; synchronized video; calibration; displacement, peak speed and settling time for every trial; mean, range and maximum; updated hazard-zone drawing. |
| V-03 | Controlled stop and supported park before de-energizing | IEC 60204-1 category 1 concept: controlled deceleration followed by power removal; an unbraked arm still requires a supported or gravity-stable final state. (pqac-00000001, pqac-00000006) | Command-to-stop time and distance; arrival at supported park; independent park confirmation; residual motion after de-energization; parking timeout or failure response. | Controller/CAN logs; supply-voltage trace; calibrated video; independent park sensor if installed; mechanical cradle or support. | At least **3 per initial pose–payload–speed condition**, including maximum reach and payload; inject each foreseeable parking timeout/failure at least once. (pqac-00000002, pqac-00000027) | Routine shutdown reaches and confirms the supported park before power opens; subsequent sag creates no pinch, spill or collision; failure produces a latched fault and prevents restart. Emergency isolation must remain immediately available. | State diagram; timeout values; initial/final joints; command, standstill, confirmation and power-off timestamps; post-power displacement; fault-injection results; configuration and software hashes. |
| V-04 | Raspberry Pi reboot and recovery test | Complete-system behavior must be tested against predetermined criteria under real-use and foreseeable-fault conditions. (pqac-00000027, pqac-00000031) | Arm and relay behavior during commanded reboot, watchdog reset, Pi power interruption, network loss and CAN loss; reboot duration; boot-time outputs; stale-command replay; reconnection and job-resume behavior. | Pi serial/system logs; CAN logger; supply/relay voltage trace; video; network capture; watchdog log. | At least **3 per failure mode**, both stationary and moving; repeat empty and at maximum intended payload in the worst gravity-loaded pose. | Reboot cannot unexpectedly remove support torque while unsupported, issue motion, replay commands or resume a job. Recovery requires deliberate local reset/start after communications, pose, payload, enclosure and safety status are verified. | Hardware/software versions; injected fault; synchronized logs and timestamps; relay/CAN states; trajectory and payload; restart steps; pass/fail and corrective action. |
| V-05 | Collision force and pressure characterization | ISO/TS 15066 body-region limits and PFL guidance; tests should reproduce risk-assessment contact scenarios using biofidelic instrumentation. Commercial devices have differed by about 5% on average and up to 10% under matched settings. (pqac-00000009, pqac-00000012, pqac-00000043) | Peak transient force and force–time curve; quasi-static force for trapping scenarios; pressure/distribution; speed, pose and contact geometry at closest-to-base or otherwise highest-effective-mass configurations. | Preferred: calibrated ≥1 kHz load cell or force gauge behind a body-region-appropriate spring/damper pad; Fuji Prescale or calibrated pressure film. Validate low-cost sensors against known loads; inexpensive resistive sensors have lost linearity above 150 N. (pqac-00000008, pqac-00000015, pqac-00000047) | **5 per contact condition** after setup qualification; use **30** for one representative condition when establishing repeatability. (pqac-00000043, pqac-00000045) | Every individual result plus measurement uncertainty remains below the applicable force and pressure limits. Otherwise reduce speed, remove sharp geometry, add padding/guarding or exclude people. A bare hobby load cell is screening evidence, not formal ISO/TS 15066 conformity evidence. | Sensor model/serial and calibration; uncertainty; sampling/filter settings; pad stiffness/damping; body region; fixture and geometry; pose, speed and payload; raw curves and film scans; peaks, mean, SD and maximum. |
| V-06 | Safety scanner/perimeter protective-stop test, if added | ISO 10218-2 safeguarding; ISO 13855 separation distance; COVR protective-stop testing. Published SDL work validated scanner-triggered stops and checked safety-zone dimensions. (pqac-00000002, pqac-00000035, pqac-00000039) | Detection and total response time; stopping time/distance; final clearance; field coverage and blind spots; warning/reduced-speed/stop sequence; clear-zone and restart interlocks. | Calibrated test piece; oscilloscope or logic analyzer; video; laser meter with stated error below 5% or motion-tracking system. (pqac-00000002) | At least **3 per approach direction, field, intrusion point, speed, pose and payload**, including boundaries, corners and foreseeable occlusions. | Worst final position plus uncertainty and margin remains within the protective separation distance; every intrusion produces the specified stop; no automatic restart; authorized restart only after the zone is clear. | Scanner configuration/checksum; field drawing; response/stopping data; final distances; test points and directions; raw traces/video; bypass and reset/restart results; approval. |
| V-07 | SOP walkthrough, training and emergency drill | Validation should cover intended use, system limits, users and training; training should include programming, troubleshooting and emergency response. (pqac-00000023, pqac-00000029, pqac-00000038) | Ability to inspect, start and stop safely; actuate E-stop; respond to sag/drop; isolate energy; clear jams safely; handle spills or broken vials; identify signage and hazards; report incidents and near misses. | Approved SOP/checklist; written and skills assessment; scenario cards; training roster; observation form; isolation hardware. | One successful walkthrough and one observed emergency drill for **every authorized user**; repeat until all critical steps pass unprompted. | All safety-critical steps completed correctly; no interlock bypass; user understands that reset does not initiate restart; only trained, named personnel operate or recover the cell; SOP and hazard analysis approved before research use. | Controlled SOP revision; trainee/instructor and dates; competency results; drill observations; authorization level; refresher date; incidents, near misses and corrective actions. |
| V-08 | Periodic and change-triggered re-verification | Risk assessment and validation should be repeated after mitigation and when tasks, environment or operators change; ongoing monitoring should include close calls, incidents and feedback. No cited standard sets one universal interval. (pqac-00000029, pqac-00000030, pqac-00000032) | Continued E-stop, interlock, park, reboot and restart performance; drift in stopping/drop/collision results; wiring/configuration changes; damage or wear; sensor contamination; training currency and incident trends. | V-01–V-07 protocols and instruments; configuration/version comparison; maintenance, training and incident logs. | Functional E-stop and interlock check **before each operating session**; documented inspection **monthly**; repeat V-01–V-04 **at least annually** and after any relevant change, repair, crash, firmware/software update or incident; repeat V-05/V-06 after geometry, speed, payload, tooling or safeguarding changes. These intervals are a defensible local policy, not quoted standard mandates. | No degraded result exceeds the approved baseline plus its stated tolerance; all safety functions pass before return to service; relevant changes trigger updated risk assessment and signed re-approval; failed tests place the cell out of service. | Master verification index; due dates; baseline and trend data; maintenance/change log; software and configuration versions; failures and corrective actions; approver signatures; next review date. |


*Table: A staged, low-cost verification plan for the BYU Vertical Cloud Lab, covering emergency stopping, gravity drop, reboot behavior, collision measurement, safeguarding, training and re-verification. It distinguishes evidence-based repetition guidance from locally proposed acceptance policies.*
